Many snails, limpets and clams have adapted to life at crushing depths in the oceans on hydrothermal vents where water temperatures can reach 450C (842F).

rfi.description: European champions Spain are on a World Cup collision course with Kylian Mbappe's France, if they can beat Belgium in the quarter-finals on Friday.

rfi.title: France must speed up climate action, as watchdog warns current efforts fall short
rfi.description: France is not prepared for the pace and scale of climate change, the country’s climate watchdog has warned in a report that calls for a significant acceleration of both emission reduction efforts and adaptation policies, as the country faces its third heatwave since May.

rfi.title: Israel's recognition of the Armenian genocide unsettles Turkey and Azerbaijan
rfi.description: Israel's parliament voted on 29 June 2026 to recognise the 1915 Armenian genocide, breaking with decades of official reticence on the issue. RFI spoke to three regional experts to unpack the politics behind the vote and its fallout: Gerald Steinberg, professor at Bar-Ilan University in Tel Aviv; Richard Giragossian, director of the Regional Studies Centre in Yerevan; and Ilter Turan, professor at Bilgi University in Istanbul.

rfi.title: Bayeux Tapestry delivered to British Museum under cover of darkness
rfi.description: After almost 1,000 years, the Bayeux Tapestry is back on English soil – spirited to London's British Museum on Friday in the dead of night, after a high-tech and high-security operation in which any slip-up could have spelled disaster.

rfi.title: Fifteen years of independence for South Sudan, but still little to celebrate
rfi.description: South Sudan, the world's youngest country, on Thursday marks the 15th anniversary of its independence, following decades of war with Sudan, a 2005 peace agreement and a 2011 self-determination referendum in which almost 99 percent of voters backed statehood. But the hopes that came with it have given way to renewed conflict, economic collapse and political deadlock.

rfi.title: Mbappé plays down injury fears after France beat Morocco to reach World Cup semis
rfi.description: France have secured a third consecutive semi-final spot, seeing off a stubborn Morocco side 2-0 on Thursday. Les Bleus missed an early spot-kick but regrouped to wear down the Atlas Lions' defence and book their place in the final four.

rfi.title: UK to lead European initiative to fund next generation of long-range missiles
rfi.description: The United Kingdom, France, Germany and other European countries will spend more than $50 billion over the next 10 years to develop long-range precision weapons in a boost to NATO's defence capabilities, the UK government announced on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Secrecy surrounds Bayeux Tapestry's imminent Channel crossing
rfi.description: Under cover of darkness and heavy police guard, the Bayeux Tapestry – a 68-metre embroidered chronicle of the Norman conquest of England, stitched in wool not long after the events it depicts – is set to cross the Channel within days, the official overseeing its move to London has revealed.

rfi.title: How appeal court verdict against Le Pen puts her back in the running for 2027
rfi.description: A French appeals court this week upheld Marine Le Pen's conviction for embezzling funds from the European Parliament and sentenced her to house arrest – something the far-right leader previously said would rule her out of France's 2027 presidential race. Yet Le Pen still has one last legal recourse to overturn her conviction and, pending that appeal, remains free to hit the campaign trail.

rfi.title: Trump says US will give Ukraine licence to build Patriot missiles
rfi.description: The United States will grant Ukraine a licence to manufacture Patriot missile interceptors domestically, President Donald Trump announced from this week's NATO summit – as Kyiv's stockpile of the US-made air defence system runs critically low amid intensifying Russian strikes.

rfi.title: Zimbabwe's ruling party accused of hollowing out parliamentary oversight
rfi.description: Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa has signed into law constitutional changes extending his time in office from 2028 to 2030. The legislation, known as CAB3, also allows parliament, rather than a public vote, to elect future presidents.

rfi.title: Western Europe records hottest ever June as climate change drives heatwaves
rfi.description: Western Europe experienced its warmest June on record, as a heatwave at the end of the month in many countries broke temperature records. The confirmation from the European Union’s climate monitor comes as many countries are facing a third heatwave this week since May.

rfi.title: 'We have our own local identity’: Morocco's Jazzablanca festival founder

euronews.description: When NATO leaders opened their gift boxes from the Turkish president and found a .357 Magnum revolver, some panicked and others laughed. euronews.title: ‘Serious concern’: Nine European countries urge EU to ease Entry/Exit System border checks
euronews.description: Airports and airlines have also joined the chorus of criticism, once again warning of the disruption caused by the Entry/Exit System (EES).

euronews.description: Around 500 firefighters, backed by Spain's Military Emergency Unit, battled to contain the flames and search for victims. Around 800 people were evacuated, including nearly 200 to temporary shelters.

lemonde.title: France-Maroc : grâce à leur attaque de feu, les Bleus qualifiés pour le dernier carré de la Coupe du monde
lemonde.description: Kylian Mbappé et ses coéquipiers ont largement dominé les Lions de l’Atlas (2-0), en confirmant leur potentiel offensif. Ils ont obtenu leur billet pour les demi-finales du Mondial, qu’ils joueront le 14 juillet, à Dallas, face à l’Espagne ou à la Belgique.

lemonde.description: Vendredi, déjà 9 départements sont en vigilance rouge, et la quasi-totalité de l’Hexagone est en orange, avec des maximales attendues en hausse. L’épisode caniculaire devrait persister au moins jusqu’au 14 juillet.

lemonde.title: Détroit d’Ormuz : Donald Trump face au risque d’une guerre sporadique contre l’Iran
lemonde.description: La reprise des frappes américaines et iraniennes, mercredi, en dépit du protocole d’accord conclu entre les deux pays compromet la perspective d’une sortie de crise rapide, alors que le conflit demeure impopulaire dans l’opinion publique américaine.

lemonde.title: Retraites : les experts du Comité de suivi préconisent de brider les pensions pour sortir d’une situation « alarmante »
lemonde.description: L’instance indépendante renouvelle sa proposition déjà formulée, et jusqu’ici refusée par les députés, de ne pas indexer l’évolution des pensions sur celle des prix jusqu’en 2030. Elle explore également l’idée d’instaurer une « règle d’or » qui permettrait de modifier automatiquement des paramètres (taux, âge…) en cas de dérapage des comptes.

lemonde.title: La tapisserie de Bayeux est arrivée au British Museum, à Londres, pour un prêt historique
lemonde.description: « C’est un moment unique, fruit d’un travail acharné, d’une planification minutieuse », s’est réjoui le directeur du British Museum, Nicholas Cullinan. La tapisserie sera exposée dans ce musée à partir du 10 septembre et jusqu’au 11 juillet 2027.

lemonde.title: Audiences radio : France Culture talonnée par Radio Nova ; France Inter, RTL et Franceinfo à la baisse
lemonde.description: Les stations généralistes ont perdu des auditeurs entre avril et juin, selon les chiffres printaniers de Médiamétrie, publiés vendredi 10 juillet. A l’exception de NRJ et Nostalgie, les musicales se portent bien.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : des accords « techniques » encore nécessaires pour la production de missiles Patriot ; un système antibalistique « équivalent » aussi en développement
lemonde.description: Le président américain, Donald Trump, avait annoncé mercredi, lors d’une rencontre avec son homologue ukrainien en marge du sommet de l’OTAN, qu’il allait autoriser Kiev à fabriquer des missiles pour ces systèmes indispensables à l’interception des missiles balistiques russes qui frappent l’Ukraine.

lemonde.title: Produits structurés dans l’assurance-vie : attention danger
lemonde.description: Portée par la volatilité des marchés financiers, la production de produits structurés aux promesses de rendement alléchantes tourne à plein régime. Ces placements vendus à l’aide d’arguments marketing simplificateurs méritent un décryptage si l’on veut s’éviter des déconvenues.

lemonde.title: France-Maroc : une adolescente est morte en célébrant la victoire des Bleus dans le Nord
lemonde.description: La jeune fille se trouvait sur l’arrière d’un camion, qui n’avait pas sa remorque, quand « elle est tombée et a été écrasée » par celui-ci, expliquent les pompiers, qui précisent qu’elle est morte sur place.

lemonde.description: Le premier secrétaire du Parti socialiste avait proposé une consultation ouverte. Les militants du PS ont, eux, choisi un vote des adhérents. Cette défaite personnelle sonne aussi la fin de la primaire unitaire de la gauche.

lemonde.title: A Porto Rico, les habitants excédés par les coupures d’eau et d’électricité à répétition
lemonde.description: Une centaine de jours sans eau ont été observés depuis le début de l’année dans le centre-ville de San Juan, en raison, notamment, du manque d’entretien du réseau, perturbant le quotidien des riverains et des commerçants.

lemonde.title: Typhon Bavi : cinq morts aux Philippines, évacuations et écoles fermées à Taïwan
lemonde.description: Le typhon Bavi, qui a déjà frappé plusieurs îles du Pacifique, doit toucher le nord et l’est de Taïwan vendredi et samedi, ainsi que les îles du sud du Japon, avant de s’abattre sur la Chine.

lemonde.description: Le parcours de la septième étape, vendredi, entre Hagetmau et Bordeaux, marque la sortie des Pyrénées avec une longue traversée des Landes et une arrivée promise aux sprinteurs.

lemonde.title: « La désindustrialisation met à mal une partie des efforts de décarbonation de la France »
lemonde.description: Le bon bilan de la France en matière de baisse des émissions de gaz à effet de serre repose en partie sur une illusion comptable : la désindustrialisation l’oblige à importer massivement des biens fortement carbonés, comme le constate une note de Rexecode, que présente Béatrice Madeline dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: A Hayange, terre d’élection de l’extrême droite, le soutien à Marine Le Pen malgré sa condamnation
lemonde.description: Dans cette petite ville mosellane, qui a réélu un maire RN au premier tour des municipales, la plupart des sympathisants du parti rencontrés jugent que le « système » s’acharne sur leur candidate.

lemonde.description: Une ambitieuse et poétique réécriture d’Homère, sous le signe de la fluidité, entre mythes antiques et errances contemporaines. Vivifiant.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Égyptiens accueillis en héros à leur retour au pays
france24fr.description: La sélection égyptienne de football a reçu un accueil triomphal vendredi à son retour au pays, où des milliers de supporters sont venus saluer son parcours historique à la Coupe du monde, achevé en huitième de finale face à l'Argentine.

france24fr.title: L'équipe égyptienne de football entourés des supporters à leur retour
france24fr.description: Des milliers de supporters égyptiens se sont rassemblés vendredi pour accueillir l’équipe nationale de football à son retour au pays. Les Pharaons, qui ont pour la première fois de leur histoire atteint les huitièmes de finale du tournoi, ont quitté l'Amérique du Nord après leur défaite 3-2 face à l’Argentine. Récit d’Étienne Paponaud.

france24fr.title: Erling Haaland : le footballeur norvégien de tous les records
france24fr.description: Il aide la #Norvège à performer au #Mondial2026 et il est considéré comme l’un des meilleurs buteurs au monde. Il s’agit de Erling Haaland. Le “cyborg” norvégien bat tous les records. Mais permettra-t-il une nouvelle victoire en quarts de finale face à l’#Angleterre ?

france24fr.title: Soudan : le difficile quotidien des habitants d'El-Obeid, encerclée par les FSR
france24fr.description: Au Soudan, l’ONU redoute un bain de sang à El-Obeid, encerclée par les Forces de soutien rapide. Environ 600 000 civils y seraient toujours piégés dans une ville à bout de souffle. Témoignage rare d’un habitant.

france24fr.title: Taïwan se prépare à l'arrivée du typhon "Bavi"
france24fr.description: Le typhon Bavi poursuit son chemin destructeur. Après avoir déjà frappé plusieurs îles du Pacifique et fait quinze morts aux Philippines, il doit toucher le nord et l'est de Taïwan vendredi et samedi, ainsi que les îles du sud du Japon, avant de s'abattre sur la Chine. Récit d’Anna Pereira.

france24fr.title: La France se prépare avec la 4e brigade d’aérocombat aux missions aériennes
france24fr.description:
Dans notre mini-série ‘La France se prépare’, embarquez avec la 4ᵉ brigade d'aérocombat pour un exercice aérien à Chaumont.  
 
Nos reporters Elisabeth Allain et Geoges Yazbeck se sont retrouvés à bord d'un NH90 Caïman, immersion au cœur d'une mission aérienne simulant l'attaque d'une cible au sol.

france24fr.title: Des entrepreneurs fortunés achètent des forêts pour ne rien en faire
france24fr.description: Ils sont millionnaires, écolos et achètent des forêts…pour surtout ne rien en faire. C'est une démarche qui gagne en popularité chez les entrepreneurs à succès : sanctuariser des domaines entiers pour protéger la biodiversité. C'est le cas du domaine du Costil, 170 hectares de forêt normande laissés en libre évolution, devenu un refuge pour des centaines d’espèces animales et végétales. C'est aussi un lieu de partage à travers les évènements de sensibilisation à la protection du vivant.

france24fr.title: Belgique ou Espagne : qui défiera la France en demi-finales du Mondial 2026 ?
france24fr.description: Les supporters français sont ravis après la victoire des Bleus face au Maroc… mais l’équipe se projette maintenant vers les demi-finales, qui annoncent un défi de taille. Le 14 juillet, jour de Fête nationale en France, la France affrontera la Belgique ou l’Espagne. Quelle ambiance sur place ? Précisions depuis Boston de Cédric Ferreira, journaliste sportif France 24.

france24fr.title: Un million de femmes et de filles privées d'aide humanitaire depuis les coupes de Trump
france24fr.description: Depuis janvier 2025 et le retour à la Maison Blanche de Donald Trump, au moins un million de femmes et de filles sont privées d'assistance en raison des coupes budgétaires dans l'aide humanitaire, alerte vendredi l'ONU Femmes. Les victimes de violences sexuelles liées aux conflits, les mères déplacées ou encore les filles contraintes de quitter l'école font partie des personnes les plus affectées, selon l'organisation.

france24fr.title: La tapisserie de Bayeux à Londres : un prêt controversé
france24fr.description: Mille ans, ou presque, après avoir raconté la conquête normande de l'Angleterre, la tapisserie de Bayeux fait de nouveau l'actualité. La broderie du XIe siècle vient d'arriver à Londres, prêtée pour la première fois de son histoire au British Museum. L'événement enthousiasme autant qu'il inquiète et rouvre un vieux débat : que vaut la diplomatie culturelle face au risque encouru par une œuvre aussi fragile ?

france24fr.title: Espagne : incendie mortel en Andalousie, plus de 500 pompiers mobilisés
france24fr.description: Prises au piège dans leur véhicule ou rattrapées par les flammes en tentant de s'enfuir à pied, au moins onze personnes, dont probablement des étrangers, ont été tuées dans une zone touristique près d'Almeria, dans le sud de l'Espagne, victimes d'un feu de forêt fulgurant.

france24fr.title: La France se prépare avec l’armée de terre en entraînement au combat urbain
france24fr.description:
À l'occasion des festivités du 14 Juillet, découvrez notre mini-série "La France se prépare". 
 
Elisabeth Allain, Georges Yazbeck et Joanna Cockerell ont suivi les exercices de haute intensité ORION 26, menés pendant deux mois par l'armée française aux côtés de ses alliés. Lors de cet épisode, ils se sont retrouvés en entraînement au combat urbain.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : comment la Norvège s'est hissée au sommet du football mondial
france24fr.description: Pour sa première Coupe du monde depuis 1998, la Norvège s'est hissée parmi les huit meilleures nations et défiera l'Angleterre samedi pour une place dans le dernier carré. Génération dorée menée par Erling Haaland, réforme structurelle et plan de jeu ambitieux… La percée des Vikings est tout sauf une surprise. Explications.

france24fr.title: L'Afrique à l'honneur aux 57e Rencontres de la photographie d'Arles
france24fr.description: Chaque été, Arles (dans le sud de la France) se transforme en une immense galerie à ciel ouvert à l'occasion des Rencontres de la photographie. Pour cette 57e édition, plus de quarante expositions investissent la ville et placent l'Afrique au cœur du festival, entre indépendances, mémoire coloniale, archives familiales et réappropriation des récits. france24fr.title: UberEats et Deliveroo suspendent les livraisons entre 14h et 18h en vigilance rouge canicule
france24fr.description: La canicule est une épreuve pour les livreurs à vélos. Sous la pression du ministre du travail, UberEats et Deliveroo, les deux leaders du secteur, ont annoncé suspendre les livraisons entre 14h et 18h dans les départements en vigilance rouge. Un premier pas en faveur de ces travailleurs précaires, qui dénoncent régulièrement leurs conditions de travail pénibles.

france24fr.title: Obsèques de Khamenei en Iran : deuil ou démonstration de force ?
france24fr.description: Les funérailles d'Ali Khamenei touchent à leur fin. L'ancien guide suprême iranien a été inhumé à Machhad, sa ville d'origine, après 6 jours de deuil national. Des milliers de personnes rassemblées sur le passage de son cercueil. Mais tandis que les échanges de frappes avec les États-Unis se poursuivent, ce moment fort à l’échelle national est-il un moment de deuil... ou une démonstration de force ? Analyse de Clément Therme, chercheur associé à l'Institut international des études iraniennes.

france24fr.title: IA : quand les robots commencent à réfléchir par eux-mêmes
france24fr.description: D'un côté, la Chine s'apprête à faire entrer, dans nos salons, des robots ultra réalistes disponibles 24h/24. De l'autre, l'IA est en train de développer sa propre "voix intérieure". C'est ce qu'Anthropic – maison mère du chatbot Claude – vient tout juste de baptiser le "J-space". Il s'agit d'une zone méconnue où l'IA manipule silencieusement des concepts avant même de formuler sa réponse. france24fr.title: Dérèglement climatique : notre cerveau, complice de l'inaction ?
france24fr.description: Épisode de chaleur extrême et multiplication des incendies dans plusieurs régions d'Europe, dont la France, frappée par une troisième canicule en moins de deux mois. Le péril climatique semble grandir bien plus vite que la transition écologique, et ce décalage a inspiré une question à Sophian Aubin, chroniqueur sciences de France 24 : notre cerveau nous condamnerait-il à l'inaction climatique ?

new-sci.title: Our fertility window could be extended by making ovaries softer
new-sci.description: A drug that softens the ovaries helped mice and rats conceive more easily at an older age, and produce more pups

new-sci.title: Lambs born via IVF using highly immature eggs in major breakthrough
new-sci.description: Lambs have been born using an experimental form of IVF that coaxes immature eggs to become mature ones. This could boost the number of eggs available for fertilisation and improve IVF success rates

new-sci.title: The allergy culprit histamine also boosts our memory
new-sci.description: A drug that raises levels of histamine – the chemical that causes allergy symptoms – in the brain boosts our memory by around 10 per cent

phys-org.description: Sometimes mistaken for a strange-looking mouse with a long, pointed snout, the Asian house shrew is a small, furry animal known for its musky odor. It's usually found lurking near homes and farms, ports and cities, across Southeast Asia, East Africa, southern Japan and islands across the Indian Ocean. phys-org.title: New Jurassic dinosaur species identified in Thailand from a single bone
phys-org.description: A new study published in Scientific Reports describes the identification of a new species of long-necked dinosaur found in the Phu Kradung Formation in Thailand. The team calls the dinosaur Uragasaurus kalasinensis and says it is the first formally named mamenchisaurid dinosaur from Thailand.

phys-org.title: Study links newspaper closures to distorted crime reporting
phys-org.description: Local newspapers serve as a vital check on public institutions, including law enforcement, according to new research from the University at Buffalo School of Management. phys-org.title: New model maps solar storms across 1 million miles around Earth
phys-org.description: A team at the Applied Physics Lab is working to understand the complex science behind predicting invisible threats that can quickly cripple electric grid infrastructure on Earth.

phys-org.title: Virtual tutoring: What started as a pandemic phenomenon has evolved from a temporary fix to an educational fixture
phys-org.description: When Amanda Neitzel first evaluated a live virtual reading-tutoring program called AirReading two years ago, she found what most educators would have predicted: modest results. One semester of live video tutoring nudged struggling early readers forward by roughly a month's worth of learning. But when she ran the study across a full school year, the difference was extraordinary. Literacy gains more than doubled.

phys-org.title: Could exoplanets locked in eternal day and endless night support life?
phys-org.description: Ever so slightly bigger than Earth, the exoplanet LHS 3844b orbits its parent star, LHS 3844, a red dwarf 48.5 light-years from our solar system. Its rotational speed mirrors its orbital speed. The result? One side of LHS 3844b is perpetually bathed in scorching sunlight, locked into a never-ending, blistering hot day, while the other is forever shrouded in darkness so cold that particles are incapable of movement, a state known as absolute zero (zero Kelvin).

phys-org.title: What happened to Australia's snow season? A climate expert explains
phys-org.description: There's nothing like gliding down a snow-covered slope. That is, if you ask the thousands of people who make an annual pilgrimage to our alpine resorts during the Australian winter. But this year, the start to the snow season has been far from spectacular.

phys-org.title: Hidden health risks found in New York City's free-roaming cats
phys-org.description: Cats may be cute and adorable, but stray and feral cats can sometimes pose a risk to human health. Veterinary researchers have discovered that more than 50% of free-roaming cats in New York City carry parasites that could potentially be transmitted to humans.

phys-org.title: 10 fathers took extended leave to care for their babies—how their family life changed
phys-org.description: The UK government launched a major review of parental leave in July 2025, with recommendations expected in early 2027. One question sits at the heart of the review: What difference does parental leave make to family life?

phys-org.title: Largest viral-protein library gives researchers new way to probe emerging pathogens
phys-org.description: To prevent viruses from sickening or killing us—whether it's an individual case of hepatitis B or a COVID pandemic—it's crucial to understand how the proteins they make initiate changes in our bodies that allow them to flourish. A new tool has broadened the scale at which researchers can study these proteins, promising to speed basic discoveries in virology, inform the development of new vaccines and treatments, and help humanity protect against emerging pathogens.

phys-org.title: Why bees are struggling to survive this summer
phys-org.description: You may be spotting dead bumblebees lying on pavements near you during the summer months. There are several reasons for this, some related to the weather and some very much due to humans.

phys-org.title: If so many people live with toxoplasmosis, how dangerous is this brain parasite really? Should I be worried?
phys-org.description: About 1 in 3 people worldwide have been infected with a microscopic parasite called Toxoplasma gondii—or simply "toxo"—which can cause toxoplasmosis. After the initial infection, toxo settles into our muscles and brains, where it can remain for life.

phys-org.title: Tiny mountain lakes pose big, overlooked flood risks, new study warns
phys-org.description: A new international study involving scientists from the University of Aberdeen has revealed a critical blind spot in global climate risk assessments—the growing danger posed by small alpine lakes formed by glacier retreat and permafrost thaw. Published in Nature Sustainability, the research highlights how these lakes, which are often too small to appear in conventional hazard databases, can still unleash sudden and destructive floods with little warning.

phys-org.title: New ligand engineering strategy creates more active nanocluster catalysts
phys-org.description: A joint research group from Tohoku University, Tokyo University of Science, Tokyo Metropolitan University and the Japan Fine Ceramics Center has developed a thermal catalyst that exhibits high carbon monoxide (CO) oxidation activity under low-temperature conditions.

phys-org.title: Rising tides, rising tensions: New research calls for rethink of coastal law
phys-org.description: As sea levels rise and coastlines erode, Australia's legal system is struggling to keep up. Longstanding assumptions about who owns the coast—and who should pay when it disappears—are now at the center of growing disputes.

phys-org.title: Warm Jupiter exoplanet transiting a sun-like star discovered
phys-org.description: An international team of astronomers reports the discovery of a new exoplanet orbiting a sunlike star as part of the Next Generation Transit Survey (NGTS). The newfound alien world, designated NGTS-39 b, is a Jupiter-sized planet with an equilibrium temperature of about 519 K. The discovery was detailed in a paper published July 2 on the preprint server arXiv.

phys-org.title: Study finds politically salient immigration issues can lead to higher industrial pollution
phys-org.description: A joint research team led by Professor Narae Lee from the School of Business and Technology Management at KAIST, in collaboration with Professor Heli Wang from Singapore Management University (SMU), analyzed immigration-related legislation and environmental data across the United States and found that when immigration becomes a central political agenda, government environmental oversight weakens and firms' toxic chemical releases increase. undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.

proj-syn.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
proj-syn.description: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.
